messages:
Olivia Nguyen: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — I think we need to nail down a compact API for demote/evict that preserves read-after-write correctness across demotions. Current handoff token stuff is getting messy across fast demotes.
Kevin Chen: Agreed. Large chunk of recent flakiness seems tied to a missing expectation check when a demote race hits in-flight writes. We keep relying on implicit sequencing. :grimacing:
Sara Patel: Can you sketch what an expectation check looks like? Is this another lease token?
Olivia Nguyen: My proposal: a tiny opt-in param on the demote call: `expected_epoch` (int) + `soft=true|false`. Demote fails fast with 409 if epochs don't match. That way callers that can tolerate failure will retry via canonical flow; callers that can't will abort.
Tariq Ali: So basically a compare-and-demote: if server epoch != expected_epoch -> reject. That avoids silent demote under a concurrent takeover. How do we acquire epoch? From the prefix metadata (generation stamp).
Kevin Chen: Right. We already maintain a `gen` per prefix; make it visible in `PrefInfo` and allow callers to read it before sensitive ops. Also we need to emit a `demote.epoch_mismatch` metric for observability.
Olivia Nguyen: Also propose `soft_demote(reason, expected_epoch)` which leaves a short-lived grace (seconds) where reads still serve from cache but new writes go to new owner. This helps streaming cursors.
Maya R.: Important: soft demote must not violate linearizability for completed writes. If a client sees ack then later reads from a new owner, they must get the write. How do we guarantee that with the grace window?
Tariq Ali: We can keep a KV tombstone-style generation: every successful write increments a `stable_gen`. A demote only proceeds when `stable_gen >= expected_gen` or we reject. For soft demote, the old owner keeps serving reads for keys with write_gen <= stable_gen. New owner accepts writes with higher gens.
Sara Patel: That sounds like two counters: `handshake_epoch` (ownership) and `stable_write_gen`. Need doc.
Kevin Chen: Implementation sketch: 1) Add `PrefInfo{epoch, stable_gen}` API. 2) Demote request: `{type: soft|hard, expected_epoch, demote_hint}`. 3) On soft demote accept: mark `epoch->epoch+1` but keep a tombstone window until `stable_gen` catches up or timeout. 4) Emit events: `demote.request`, `demote.accept`, `demote.fail`, `demote.finalize`.
infra-bot: deploy-batch triggered by Olivia:deploy/demote-api-spike -> k8s job rr=2 -> started
Kevin Chen: For safety, can we add an HTTP header `X-Demote-Hint` that routes long-lived cursors to old owner for TTL seconds? That keeps logic out of hot path.
Olivia Nguyen: Good call. Also P0 test: simulate streaming request that writes mid-stream and then owner demotes -> verifying read-after-write holds. I'll add a small chaos test: `./tools/chaos/demote_smoke.sh` (pseudo):
```
# demote_smoke.sh
curl -X POST /prefix/claim -> gets epoch E
start stream write (msg1)
curl -X POST /admin/demote -d '{"expected_epoch":E, "type":"soft"}'
finish write
assert subsequent reads see msg1
```
Tariq Ali: Rollout plan: feature-flag `kv.demote_api_v2`. Start internal canary on a single shard, run chaos test and perf bench (latency p95) for 48h, then stagger across zones.
Sara Patel: What about metrics/alerts? Proposed: alerts on `demote.fail.rate > 0.5%` and `demote.finalize.latency > 30s` and increase in read error rate after demote.
Maya R.: Also track `demote.soft.window_missed` to catch cases where stable_gen didn't catch up before timeout. That should surface customer-impacting regressions.
Kevin Chen: Edge-case: dual demote racing -> both nodes could accept a demote if expected_epoch matches concurrently. Use CAS on epoch field to avoid double-accept.
Olivia Nguyen: Yep CAS + durability write. We also need storage-level atomic op for epoch bump or use raft leader. Implementation detail for later.
ops-bot: Note created: RFC follow-up doc draft in /docs/internal/kv-demote-api.md (draft 0.1)
Olivia Nguyen: I'll draft the doc with diagrams + state machine table. Assigning follow-ups: Kevin - add PrefInfo API; Tariq - implement CAS/telemetry; Sara - tests & canary; Maya - SRE runbook & alerts.
Kevin Chen: I'll open a PR by EOD with interface proto and a minimal server-side guard.
Sara Patel: I'll wire the chaos test into CI canary and post results here.
Olivia Nguyen: Thanks all. If anyone sees a corner I missed ping me. :+1:
